patch_description: The low pre-repair feasible rate suggests that the degree penalty is too weak relative to the accumulated link rewards. A link can participate in many quadratic terms, so comparing the penalty only with the largest individual QUBO coefficient understates its possible influence. Estimate the largest per-link objective change from its linear term and all incident quadratic terms, after accounting for the evaluator’s weight normalization, and set the penalty just above half that bound. A single-bit change from a valid topology changes two degree counts, incurring a penalty increase of twice the penalty weight; this makes such a change unattractive while keeping the penalty demand- and size-adaptive.
